# M0 spec — notes for the build waves' item checkers (lane build/m0-check-close-r4, 2026-10-03)

These are observations from the closing check of the M0 spec. None of them blocks the spec under the session's closing
rule (J160). A blocker is a compile or dependency cycle, an item that cannot be built inside its `owns`, a dependency or
wave-order violation, a timing-phase conflict, a clean-room breach, or a command that exits non-zero. The closing
check's one blocker is reported in its structured result as SP-r4-01; it is not repeated here. Each item's checker
reads the rows for its item as it checks the item against its design sections. Rows are append-only: a later
observation is a new row.

| id | item | observation | suggested handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| N-01 | M0-f-02b | The first test asserts each job's derived status on the real manifests: *built* for every M0 job, and *after-M-1 naming its file* for the deny-list scan and the parity report. Under C-0121, M0-k-07 may review `denylist.json` in any build wave once the list crosses, which can be before wave 18. M0-b-05a and M0-c-07a review `baselines.json` after M0-x-01. Once either review lands, that job derives *built* and the assertion turns `corepack pnpm test` red. C-0105 also says vitest tests run over fixture manifests only. | Derive the statuses over a fixture tree. Alternatively, accept for each M-1-file job any status in the set {`after-M-1: <file>`, `after-M-1: <file> (review pending: <item>)`, `built`}. The checker runs the test with the reviewer's summary planted and with it absent. |
| N-02 | M0-k-05, C-0120 | C-0120 (2) holds back only the *numbers-only* crossings until M0-k-05 has LANDED. A digest file may therefore cross in waves 2–10, before M0-k-05 creates `crossings.json` as `[]`. Its countersigner would then create M0-k-05's owned file by appending. `verify.mjs` accepts a rewrite of an append file by its owner as "edited beyond appends, claimed whole", reported as a note and not a failure. So if M0-k-05's builder rewrote the file as `[]`, the earlier records would be lost and the check would still pass. | M0-k-05's checker confirms that every record present before the landing survives it. Alternatively, a choices row makes digest crossings also wait for M0-k-05, as the numbers-only files do. |
| N-03 | M0-b-05a, M0-c-07b | M0-b-05a re-runs M0-b-04's harness (T34-1's 10 000-face mean with the new depth rows). M0-c-07b re-runs the gate through M0-c-06's harness. Each harness writes its numbers-only summary to `docs/build/summaries/M0-b-04.json` or `M0-c-06.json`. The run items do not own those files, so `landed:verify` would name them unattributed. | The harnesses write their `plat/` summary only when the owning item passes an explicit flag (for example `--summary`). A re-run by a run item writes to `PLAT_BENCH_OUT`, and the run item quotes the numbers in its own summary. M0-b-04's and M0-c-06's checkers confirm the flag. |
| N-04 | M0-e-03 | `dependsOn` names M0-x-02 (the layout pipeline). Site code cannot import `@plat/layout` (§14), and the site test project references only kernel, model and tables. If the S1 stage test runs through M0-x-02's runner, it cannot compile in `site/test/water/`. | Test the stage with a hand-built `StageContext` (the model's type), and drop or explain the M0-x-02 dependency. Any runner-based run belongs to M0-x-04 or M0-e-06. |
| N-05 | M0-a-02 | Its `interfaces` list `PlatKey` and `LatticeSpec`. These are M0-a-01's (`kernel/src/types`, `kernel/src/num`; C-0112). A second declaration in `kernel/src/arena` would give TS2308 through `kernel/src/index.ts`'s `export *` lines. | Import them, and re-export the same symbol if needed, never redeclare. The checker greps `arena/` for the two declarations. |
| N-06 | M0-k-05 | Beside C-0116's ⟨M-1⟩ rule, the builds keep "a KS row without spreadKS → missingBaseline". The spec does not state the verdict for an `m1` distribution row (blocks, cut lengths per face) that exists but lacks `spreadKS`. | The item picks the verdict and records it in a choices row. *fail* is the reading closer to §13.5's ⟨M-1⟩ rule. Add one test for that case. |
| N-07 | M0-k-05 | R4 is measured on block OBB axes, which uses M0-a-10's `obb`. M0-a-10 is not in `dependsOn`. The wave order still holds (wave 4 before wave 11). | Add the dependency for the record; no schedule change. |
| N-08 | M0-c-05 | Its *here* bar (no turn cliff, the junction row, growth drift on 1 000 seeds) uses the metric definitions of M0-k-05, which lives in testkit and which `layout/test` cannot import (see SP-r4-01). Writing the measurement again in the item's own test would risk a second `metricVersion`. | Run these clauses where testkit is visible: the testkit test folder SP-r4-01's fix assigns, or M0-c-06's harness, whose bar already carries them. |
| N-09 | M0-f-02b, M0-t-01 | "M0-t-01 requires every M0 job built before it times a tier" sits beside C-0121's pending jobs, which are listed in the tier record and never timed. | Read the sentence as "every job not pending on an M-1 file". M0-t-00's fixture test already holds a pending job. |
| N-10 | M0-k-07 | When the list crosses after M0-x-01, a true reuse found by M0-k-07 is fixed in the owning item's fix round *after* the timing record. The record's code is then no longer the code that was timed. | M0-x-03's addendum lists every fix round taken after M0-x-01 and re-runs the touched items' non-timing tests. A fix that touches a timed loop is flagged for M1's first timing phase. |
| N-11 | (the validator) | The checkers' validator (`scratchpad/build/check-r3/validate.py`) still reports two expected cases: AFTER-M-1 (b)'s stated sequence (M0-b-05b → M0-c-07b → M0-x-03), and M0-k-07 without an M0-x-01 dependency (C-0121's design). It also reports the scaffold's generic `<module>` and `<harness>` index entries as overlaps. | Encode the three exceptions in the validator, so that any new line is a real problem. Add a rule: a test that names a testkit item's code lies in a test project that references `@plat/testkit` (SP-r4-01). |
| N-12 | M0-d-07 | *(close-r5)* C-0122 puts six package items' tests under `packages/testkit/test/<package>/<folder>/`. The lint M0-d-07 builds must treat these files as test-kit code, not as the package named in the path. A lint that recognised packages by a `kernel/` or `layout/` path segment would apply the model-package rules and the dependency-direction rule to them, refuse their `@plat/testkit` and oracle imports, and fail `corepack pnpm lint` for all six items. The scaffold's empty lint passes such files (CONFIRMED in a scratch copy: 118 files, 0 errors). | Classify a file by the folder directly under `packages/`, so anything under `packages/testkit/` is test-kit code at every depth. Add one pass fixture: a file under `testkit/test/kernel/<folder>/` importing `@plat/kernel`, `@plat/testkit` and `polygon-clipping`. M0-d-07's checker runs it. |
| N-13 | M0-a-08 | *(close-r5)* The scaffold's header comment in `kernel/src/arr/index.ts` still says the index belongs to M0-a-09. Since C-0122 / C-0123 the file goes to M0-a-08 at wave 8 and passes to M0-a-09 at wave 9. The attribution tools already follow this hand-over. CONFIRMED in a scratch copy: `landed -- M0-a-08` after a wave-8 snapshot and `landed -- M0-a-09` after a wave-9 snapshot each claimed their edit of the file, and `landed:verify` exited 0 both times. | M0-a-08 corrects the comment when it writes its five lines. Its checker reads "exactly its five re-export lines" as those five lines plus the header comment. |
| N-14 | M0-a-08, M0-a-09 | *(close-r5)* The oracle-agreement tests ask for at least 10⁵ unattracted cases per operation (§13.1's vacuity guard). A vitest property runs `PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS` cases, 10⁴ when unset (the PR size, C-0057), so the guard cannot hold at that size. Asserted literally, it turns `corepack pnpm test` red. | The item picks the rule and records it in a choices row. Suggested: assert the 10⁵ guard only when `PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS` is at least 10⁵, as in the nightly 10⁶ run (M0-k-04's B-FUZZ job); at the PR size, assert a minimum unattracted share and report the count. The checker runs the test at both sizes. |
| N-15 | M0-k-03 (C-0124 (2)) | *(close-r5)* The `types` file that `clipper2-wasm` 0.4.0 declares is missing from its tarball. CONFIRMED in a scratch copy: a local `declare module 'clipper2-wasm'` in `testkit/src/oracles/` lets `corepack pnpm build` exit 0, and vitest loads the module (its default export is a function). A hand-written `.d.ts` in `src/` is not emitted into the test kit's declaration output. An adapter that leaked a library type into its exported signature still built in the probe. | Type the adapter's exports with our own types, so `testkit/test` and the bench never lean on the unemitted declaration. M0-k-03's checker runs `tsc -b` and confirms that no `any` comes from the import, as C-0124 states. |
| N-16 | M0-a-01, M0-a-04, M0-a-05, M0-a-07, M0-a-10, M0-a-13, M0-a-14, M0-d-04 | *(close-r5)* These items' B-FUZZ lines name no test-kit item or test-kit code, and none of these items depends on one. M0-a-01 lands before M0-k-01 (wave 4), and M0-a-04, M0-a-05 and M0-a-10 land before M0-k-02 (wave 7). Each line can be met by the item's own fast-check properties in its kernel test folder, where fast-check is visible (CONFIRMED by close-r4). M0-k-04's runner (wave 11) applies M0-a-14's checks and the Euler characteristic to M0-k-01's and M0-k-02's arenas. M0-d-09 runs M0-d-04's full-recompute oracle over the spike runs. | Each checker reads these lines as the item's own arbitraries. A builder who reads "every B-FUZZ arena" or "the fuzz runs" as the test kit's arenas moves that test, under C-0122, to `testkit/test/kernel/<folder>/` in the item's `owns`, adds M0-k-01 and M0-k-02 to `dependsOn` (only where both land in an earlier wave), and records the move in a choices row. |

That validator (`build/fix5/validate.py`) and this check's independent visibility check (`build/close-r5/vis.py`) live in the session scratchpad.
